**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:10591)

Gain-of-function variants in SCN4A lead to disrupted skeletal muscle sodium channel activity, manifesting as myotonia and episodic weakness in both diseases.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of distinct causal genes for MONDO:0013234 and potassium-aggravated myotonia, or evidence that the shared SCN4A variants associated with one disease are loss-of-function while those for the other are gain-of-function. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in SCN4A can facilitate the development of targeted therapies for both conditions, potentially by modulating sodium channel activity.

Gain-of-function mutations in SCN4A and SCN1A lead to increased voltage-gated sodium channel activity, contributing to epilepsy. Gain-of-function mutations in CACNA1A lead to increased voltage-gated calcium channel activity, contributing to migraine.
